clue.text: Specimen politician found in Manchester suburb

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Sale is a town on the southern edge of Greater Manchester
MP, Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword politician

explanation.surface: A typical politician turns up in a suburb of Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Sale is a town on the southern edge of Greater Manchester, England; 'found in' puts the politician inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is an example taken to show what the whole is like, a synonym.

clue.text: Little by little taken in by a fellow over the herring-pond

indicators.note: a thing taken in by another is held inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Eric, or, Little by Little is a Victorian school novel by F. W. Farrar, so its subtitle stands for its title, Eric

explanation.surface: Something is absorbed gradually by a chap living across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little by little' looks like an adverb meaning gradually, but it is the subtitle of Farrar's novel 'Eric, or, Little by Little', so it gives ERIC. 'The herring-pond' is a jocular name for the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring-pond is a humorous name for the North Atlantic, so from Britain the United States lies over it.

clue.text: Contrary appears by means of poetry

parts.note: per is Latin-derived English for by means of, as in 'per post'
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Something seems unexpected when expressed in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means obstinately going against what is wanted, which is being contrary.

clue.text: Fine feathers for one in retirement

definitions.text: Fine feathers for one in retirement

parts.words: Fine feathers for one in retirement
parts.note: retirement here is going to bed, and the fine feathers are the soft down of a duck used to fill a bed quilt

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests giving up work, but it means retiring for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: This quilt is filled with the soft breast feathers of a sea duck and covers a sleeper in bed.

clue.text: Open a knife, being heartless, and get past

parts.note: overt means open, done in plain view

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone unfolds a knife, callously, and moves ahead of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being heartless' strips the middle NIF from 'knife', leaving KE.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake a vehicle is to catch up with and pass it, a synonym.

clue.text: Friendly man — keeps rings to adjust

indicators.note: to adjust is to rearrange, so the letters of the preceding words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A man retains his rings so that he can resize them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjust' rearranges all of MAN KEEPS RINGS TO, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people still on these terms are friendly enough to talk, an idiom.

clue.text: A university's interpretation

explanation.surface: The way an academic institution reads something.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town in Berkshire, England, with its own university.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the English town with a university; the other is a particular understanding of a text or event.

clue.text: At 50 the worker in charge needs a lot of water

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: At fifty, the supervising employee needs plenty to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The second-largest ocean is certainly a great deal of water, an understatement.

clue.text: To charm one's way in

explanation.surface: How to beguile someone into letting you in.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable it is a verb meaning to enchant; on the first, a noun for a door or opening.

clue.text: Governor's bringing in his new wife to the islands

indicators.note: bringing something in puts it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor, and 's stands for is
a bride is a newly married wife

explanation.surface: A colonial governor brings his recently married wife to some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: His Excellency is the formal style of a colonial governor, and the 's is read as 'is'. The islands lie off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of islands off Scotland's west coast is known collectively by this name, a proper-name example.

clue.text: The case is damp and everything inside

indicators.note: a piece said to be inside another sits within its letters

parts.note: wet means damp
all means everything

explanation.surface: The suitcase has got wet, along with all its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a small flat case for notes and cards, so a kind of holder.

clue.text: A story about satisfied engineers in the plant

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes round it

parts.note: a lie is a story, an untrue tale
to meet a demand is to satisfy it, so satisfied gives met
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A tale about engineers who were contented at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is a tree. RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden is a broadleaf tree, a growing thing and so a plant.

clue.text: City girl returning after six

indicators.note: coming after something places this piece later in the answer

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: a returning word travels backwards, so the girl's name is written right to left

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A town girl comes back home after six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria's capital is a major European city, an example.

clue.text: Hoarding hosiery?

explanation.surface: Is the person laying in supplies buying socks?
explanation.definitionFit: Stocking means building up a store of goods; it is also a close-fitting leg garment.

clue.text: Louvres refitted in New York with some trepidation

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it
something refitted is put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Window slats being replaced in a Manhattan building with some anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refitted' rearranges the letters of 'Louvres' into ERVOUSL; 'in' puts that inside the New York abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with trepidation is acting anxiously, the adverb's sense.

clue.text: Long ago — and never again!

explanation.surface: Something happened in the distant past and will not be repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: It means at some former time; as an exclamation it means only one time, so never again.

clue.text: Wholly at fault over claim

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece over another stands above it, so comes first

parts.note: out means in error, as in 'your sums are out'
a right is a claim, an entitlement

explanation.surface: Someone is completely wrong about an entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely and without reservation, a synonym.

clue.text: "What we behold is — by our eyes" (Marlowe)

definitions.text: "What we behold is — by our eyes" (Marlowe)

parts.words: "What we behold is — by our eyes" (Marlowe)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Marlowe's Hero and Leander: the missing word means judged

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Christopher Marlowe's poem Hero and Leander, just before 'Whoever loved, that loved not at first sight?'
explanation.definitionFit: Hero and Leander's line uses this verb in its old sense of judged, the word filling the gap.

clue.text: Pain in the stomach everyone suffers

indicators.note: letters in a phrase are found running across its words

explanation.surface: Everyone gets a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'stomACH Everyone'. The surface plants a stomach ache to make it look like the definition's context.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuing pain, a synonym.

clue.text: Flowering plant, a creeper, brought up under house

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece under another comes after it

parts.note: an asp is a snake, a creature that creeps

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: led means brought, as in 'led him home'

explanation.surface: A climbing plant was raised beneath the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creeper' looks like a climbing plant, but it is the snake ASP. LED (brought) read upwards gives DEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family plant with flower spikes, an example.

clue.text: The rune is complicated with cipher to this

indicators.note: letters that are complicated are tangled up, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a cipher is a zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: An ancient letter is hard to read when written in code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is complicated' rearranges THE RUNE into HEREUNT; 'cipher' looks like code, but means nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereunto is a formal word meaning to this document or matter, a synonym.

clue.text: Catches resulting from nearness

indicators.note: the answer results from the word nearness, which is rearranged to produce it

explanation.surface: Being close leads to someone being trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to trap, so the verb form means catches.

clue.text: Egghead behind Oriental

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter, E
astern means behind, in sailing terms

explanation.surface: An intellectual is trailing a person from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it is the head of 'egg', E.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means of the East, a synonym.

clue.text: Oppose one's inclusion among the others

parts.note: the rest means the others
one is I, and 's stands for is, giving I'S

explanation.surface: A person objects to being grouped with everybody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', I + S, and 'inclusion among' sets that inside the word for the others, just before its last letter.

clue.text: Paid attention to authorization by male journalist

parts.note: OK is approval or authorization
he is the male pronoun
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.definitionFit: To take heed is to pay careful attention, an idiom.

clue.text: An order to keep up 13

explanation.walkthrough: 13 is STOCKING (13 across). The Order of the Garter is England's senior order of knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the oldest English order of chivalry, and also a band worn to hold a stocking up.

clue.text: What this occupant pays to hold a party

clue.text: Constituents insisted there be good order

explanation.surface: Voters demanded that there be law and order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' looks like voters, but it signals the letters of 'insisted' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is the state of being neat and well arranged, a synonym.

clue.text: Cowardly plot getting Malvolio to wear these 13s
